title: Word Search

statement.hi:
Ek `m x n` characters ka grid `board` aur ek string `word` diya hai. Agar `word` grid me exist karta hai to `true` return karo, warna `false`.

Word ko **adjacent** cells (upar/neeche/left/right) ke letters se banana hai, aur ek cell ek word me **ek se zyada baar** use nahi ho sakta.
statement.en:
Given an `m x n` grid of characters `board` and a string `word`, return `true` if `word` exists in the grid, otherwise `false`.

The word must be built from letters of **sequentially adjacent** cells (horizontally or vertically neighbouring), and the same cell may **not be used more than once**.

constraints: board and word consist only of English letters (upper and lower case)

hi: Har cell ko starting point maan ke DFS try karo.
DFS me cell ko temporarily "visited" mark karo aur wapas aate waqt unmark karo (backtrack).
en: Try a DFS starting from every cell.
In the DFS, mark the cell as visited temporarily and unmark it on the way back (backtrack).

explain.hi: "B" wala cell dobara use karna padega, jo allowed nahi.
explain.en: It would need to reuse the "B" cell, which is not allowed.

approach.hi:
Har cell `(i, j)` se `dfs(i, j, k)` chalao: agar `board[i][j] == word[k]` hai to cell ko `#` se mark karo, chaaron neighbours me `k + 1` dhoondo, phir original letter wapas rakho.
`k == word.length` matlab poora word mil gaya.
Time O(m · n · 3^L) (L = word length), extra space O(L) recursion.
approach.en:
From every cell `(i, j)` run `dfs(i, j, k)`: if `board[i][j] == word[k]`, mark the cell with `#`, look for `k + 1` in the four neighbours, then restore the letter.
`k == word.length` means the whole word was matched.
Time O(m · n · 3^L) (L = word length), extra space O(L) for recursion.
